#
# The feature combinations CI lints one at a time, each with its tests
# (`cargo clippy --no-default-features --features X --tests -- -D warnings`;
# for `wasm`, `cargo check --target wasm32-unknown-unknown --lib`).
# `--all-features` turns everything on and the no-features clippy step turns
# everything off, so a break that appears only with SOME features off is
# found here and nowhere else.
#
# ci.yml's `features` job runs these in a few jobs, through
# `scripts/check-feature-matrix.py --group I --groups N`, and the same script
# with no arguments lints them all locally. Format: the features, then
# optionally `suite` (run the whole test suite with them), `lib` (run the
# library's unit tests with them) or `test=NAME` (run that test target with
# them). A `test=` is a test that exists only where a
# feature is ABSENT: `--all-features` and the pre-commit hook's
# `--features full` compile it out, and the lint builds it without running
# it, so this is the one place it runs.
#
# `hook` marks a row that .githooks/pre-push also lints before every push,
# with the same clippy command, under a pass stamp of its own. The
# pre-commit hook builds only `--features full`: in pull request #763 a
# binding read only under `#[cfg(feature = "hep")]` passed it, and would have
# failed this lint in CI for every set without `hep`. Three rows carry the
# mark: `native` (no `hep`, no `tls`, no `tui`), the default features, and
# the headless recipe. Measured on the aarch64 development host on
# 2026-11-12, at a load average of 23 to 30: the three together took 49 s
# after a change to src/lib.rs alone, 91 s in an earlier run of the same
# kind, and 163 s the first time after edits to test files; a stamped row is
# skipped. A marked row cannot carry `needs=`. The mark changes nothing in
# CI. scripts/tests/test_feature_matrix_hook_rows.py holds the rule.
#
# scripts/tests/test_feature_matrix_groups.py holds the list to every
# combination and test CI checked on 2026-11-03.

# The documented headless server build (README "Headless capture host"), with
# its full test suite, so the exact set users are told to ship stays green.
native,hep,api,mcp,mcp-http suite hook
# Feature-gate refusals: no mcp and no hep.
native test=feature_gate_test hook
tls
api
# mcp without mcp-http.
mcp test=app_servers_test
hep
# Standalone metrics server must build without the `api` feature.
metrics
tls,api
native,tui,audio
# The crate's default features, what a bare `cargo build` produces.
# the_feature_matrix_includes_the_default_feature_set keeps this equal to
# Cargo.toml's `default = [...]`. `lib`, because a bare `cargo test` runs the
# library's unit tests with these features and CI ran them only with every
# feature on: a popup gate that failed without `archive` sat on main unseen.
native,tui,audio,metrics lib hook
# TUI snapshots without audio.
native,tui,tls,hep,api test=tui_snapshot_test
# The eBPF uprobe backend, which every published *-linux-gnu binary carries.
# Its USERSPACE half is what this compiles: the kernel half needs nightly and
# bpf-linker, which the release job installs and this one deliberately does
# not, so build.rs takes its degrading default and emits the placeholder
# object. This proves the `#[cfg(feature = "bpf")]` code and its tests still
# build, and `a_release_build_refuses_to_ship_without_the_kernel_programs`
# proves the release cannot ship the placeholder.
bpf
# vCon export, and its rules without opus. In `full`, so `--all-features`
# already builds it; this proves it still builds WITHOUT tui, tls, api or
# mcp, the class of break `--all-features` cannot see.
vcon test=vcon_rules_test
# Ogg Opus recordings: libopus, compiled with cmake. In `full`; this proves it
# builds with only `vcon` beside it.
opus needs=cmake
# `audio` and `plugins` are each in `full` and so built by `--all-features`,
# but never ALONE: a `#[cfg(feature = "audio")]` or `"plugins"` block that
# leans on a sibling feature for an import compiles there and nowhere else.
audio
plugins
# Password-protected ZIP input. In `full`; this proves it builds without tui,
# tls, api or mcp, the only company it keeps being `native`.
archive
# G.729 decoding. In `full`; this proves it builds with only `native` beside
# it, without the `vcon` HTTPS client that the online `sipnab g729 install`
# uses.
g729
# The sets release.yml publishes: the static musl tarballs, and the gnu
# `-noaudio` .deb/.rpm with `bpf` added.
# ci_compiles_every_reduced_feature_set_the_release_publishes keeps these
# equal to what release.yml computes.
native,tui,tls,hep,api,mcp,mcp-http,metrics,archive,g729
native,tui,tls,hep,api,mcp,mcp-http,metrics,archive,g729,bpf
# The library for wasm32.
wasm needs=wasm32
